subject: Pilot qualification: Concordant Systems trial metrics & ops alignment
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@concordant.ai>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@concordant.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot qualification: Concordant Systems trial metrics & ops alignment

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — good discussion. As promised, here’s a concise post-call recap and a concrete proposal for the pilot acceptance criteria and operational responsibilities so we can get internal approvals and a procurement timeline nailed down. I pulled in Ben and Marissa for ops / success ownership.

Objective: 4-week trial to validate production inference economics and latency/quality across two representative workloads ("search summarization" and "customer reply generation").

Proposed success metrics (initial):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 512-token requests (single-shard, host-config) and p95 <= 350ms for 2k token tail cases under target concurrency.
- Throughput: sustained 120 QPS per model shard for the search workload with <5% error rate.
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.0025 / token (end-to-end measured including batching/overhead).
- Quality: automated eval on your held-out set: ROUGE-L >= 0.52 for summarization; intent-classification F1 >= 0.86 for reply routing.
- Stability: <1% of requests hit fallback model variant or regional failover during the pilot window.

Operational plan / owners:
- Redwood (Ben): environment provisioning, baseline performance runbook, and tokenized cost report cadence (weekly).
- Concordant (Priya / Alex): supply sample workloads (10k de-identified examples), define quality thresholds for the two workloads, and provide a secure S3 read-only bucket + IAM role for trial data.
- Marissa: onboarding for your SRE and a 30-min training on console dashboards and incident playbook.

Timeline (target):
- Day 0–3: contract signature + account provisioning + access exchange (S3 IAM).
- Day 4–10: baseline smoke tests and warmup (latency/throughput tuning).
- Day 11–24: measurement window (steady-state runs + evaluation).
- Day 25–28: readout, artifacts (cost/latency/quality report), and decision go/no-go.

Requirements / asks for kickoff:
1) Provide the 10k sample records (anonymized) and a short doc describing tokenization/expected sequence lengths by EOD Wed.
2) Confirm the procurement/PO owner and if any legal review is needed to get to Day 0.
3) Provide the names of your SRE and compliance contact for the security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence request).

I attached a quick stub spreadsheet with the acceptance metric buckets so we can iterate. Ben / Marissa — flag anything we should change before Priya signs off.

Next steps: Priya to confirm data delivery timeline; we’ll aim to start Day 0 by next Monday if procurement allows.

Thanks —
Sofia

Sofia —

Thanks for the thorough recap and proposed criteria. This is very helpful. Quick clarifications from our side before we commit: 

1) For cost, your note says $0.0025 / token — can Redwood provide the expected variance if we enable 8-bit quantization vs float16? We want a conservative procurement forecast.
2) For the 10k sample set — we will sanitize PII but expect ~20% of samples to be >1k tokens. That will likely push the tail latency numbers. Can we add an observational threshold for 2k+ cases (e.g., p95 <= 450ms) instead of a hard failure gate?
3) Security: we can share an S3 bucket and a compliance contact (Lina Roberts). We will need the standard SOC2 attestation and a pointer to your data retention settings for the trial.

Procurement: PO owner is our procurement lead (CFO loop); tentative go/no-go is next Friday pending legal checklist.

If that looks OK, Alex and I can sign the kick-off email and deliver the dataset on Wed as requested.

Best,
Priya
Head of Product, Concordant Systems
priya@concordant.ai

Looping in Jordan for capacity planning and Marissa for onboarding. Notes from my side: 

- Quantization delta: we typically see 10–25% cost reduction with int8/8-bit quant but p95 latency can increase slightly depending on kernel path. I recommend we present two cost scenarios in the kickoff: (1) conservative float16 baseline cost and (2) optimized int8 expected cost. I’ll prepare a short table.
- Tail latencies: agree to add an observational soft gate for >=2k tokens: p95 <= 450ms is reasonable as an observation threshold; hard gate remains the 512-token p95 <= 200ms.
- Data delivery: confirm S3 read-only + sample manifest (CSV) with tokenized length column. We need the manifest to route the workload into the right batch buckets.
- Security stub: I attached the standard network-security-evidence-stub we give prospects (contains pointers to SOC2 report and control summaries). We cannot attach the full SOC2 here, but legal can provide an NDA+SOC2 access link once PO is in place.

Action items (internal):
- Ben: create cost scenarios and small-run benchmark by Wed EOD.
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min console onboarding and audit the account ACLs (T+2 days).
- Jordan: reserve a two-shard test pool and confirm autoscale min capacity.

I’ll add these as a checklist in our deal record (DEAL-9082).

Thanks —
Ben
